questions.question: He was introduced…….the director by his friend.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after 'introduced' when referring to a person is 'to'.

questions.question: The assembly hall was so crowded……. people that he could not find a seat.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'crowded with'.

questions.question: I have been in this school…….three years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration of time.

questions.question: The accident occurred………the driver's mistake.
questions.explanation: 'Through' indicates the cause of something.

questions.question: The aeroplane was …….. by the missile.
questions.explanation: 'Hit' is the correct past participle in this passive construction.

questions.question: Asi is the …… of the triplets.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'tallest' is used when comparing three or more people.

questions.question: The puppy is…….young to eat meat.
questions.explanation: 'Too' is used in the 'too...to' construction.

questions.question: Neither Peter nor Paul …….willing to wash the car.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearest subject (Paul, singular).

questions.question: You can go home alone,……..?
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag.

questions.question: The hole was …….. by me.
questions.explanation: 'Dug' is the correct past participle of 'dig'.

questions.question: The ……. are troublesome.
questions.explanation: The plural verb 'are' requires the plural noun 'students'.

questions.question: There is …….water left in the fridge.
questions.explanation: 'A little' is used with uncountable nouns like 'water'.

questions.question: If you had come earlier, you ……met John.
questions.explanation: Third conditional requires 'would have + past participle'.

questions.question: There is too…….noise here!
questions.explanation: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like 'noise'.

questions.question: Can you account ……..your absence? Asked the headmaster.
questions.explanation: 'Account for' is the correct phrasal verb.

questions.question: Have you got enough money to build a house?
questions.explanation: 'Sufficient' is nearest in meaning to 'enough'.

questions.question: We can all expect to encounter difficulties in life.
questions.explanation: 'Meet' is nearest in meaning to 'encounter'.

questions.question: All the old houses were pulled down.
questions.explanation: 'Demolished' is nearest in meaning to 'pulled down'.

questions.question: Washing here is prohibited.
questions.explanation: 'Forbidden' is nearest in meaning to 'prohibited'.

questions.question: Adwoa went to purchase a new bag for her birthday party.
questions.explanation: 'Buy' is nearest in meaning to 'purchase'.

questions.question: Akua is a pain in the neck. This means that Akua is a………
questions.explanation: 'A pain in the neck' means an annoying person.

questions.question: I couldn't make head or tail of what he was saying. This means that……..
options: A. his drawing was not clear
B. I did not see him clearly
C. I did not understand what he was saying
D. what he was saying made me dizzy
questions.explanation: 'Couldn't make head or tail of' means unable to understand.

questions.question: Frema has a heart of gold. This means that she is ………
questions.explanation: 'Heart of gold' means very kind and generous.

questions.question: Efua's mother is the breadwinner of the family. This means that Efua's mother……….
options: B. is a very good baker
questions.explanation: 'Breadwinner' means the person who earns money to support the family.

questions.question: The teacher wants the message to be recorded in black and white. This means the message should be …..
questions.explanation: 'In black and white' means written down or printed.

questions.question: All his arrows hit the target.
questions.explanation: 'Missed' is the opposite of 'hit'.

questions.question: The fruit is sour.
questions.explanation: 'Sweet' is the opposite of 'sour'.

questions.question: There is a foul smell in the area.
questions.explanation: 'Pleasant' is the opposite of 'foul'.

questions.question: The twins are similar in appearance.
questions.explanation: 'Different' is the opposite of 'similar'.

questions.question: The large fortune Otu inherited from his uncle has been a blessing to him.
questions.explanation: 'Curse' is the opposite of 'blessing'.

questions.question: The first railways were built in the early 19th century and were powered by steam (31) ______.
questions.explanation: Steam engines powered early railways.

questions.question: These early trains were (32) ______ by horses, but soon, steam locomotives took over.
questions.explanation: 'Powered by' means operated by.

questions.question: Railways allowed for faster travel and more (33) ______ transport of goods.
questions.explanation: 'Rapid' means fast, fitting the context of improved transport.

questions.question: One of the most notable (34) ______ in railway history was the opening of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway.
questions.explanation: 'Milestones' means important achievements.

questions.question: It was the first railway to rely exclusively on steam power, carry both (35) ______ and goods.
questions.explanation: 'Passengers' is the standard term for people travelling on trains.

questions.question: and have a (36) ______ timetable.
questions.explanation: A 'fixed timetable' means a set, regular schedule.

questions.question: This railway set the standard for modern railways and (37) ______ many innovations in the field.
questions.explanation: 'Inspired' means to stimulate new ideas.

questions.question: with the introduction of diesel and electric (38) ______.
questions.explanation: 'Locomotives' are railway engines.

questions.question: offering speeds that can compete with air travel.
questions.explanation: 'Limits' refers to pushing the boundaries of speed.

questions.question: Today, railways continue to play a crucial role in (40) ______ connectivity.
questions.explanation: 'Increasing' connectivity means improving links.

questions.question: If it rained, the farmer _____ his seeds.
questions.explanation: Second conditional (if + past simple, would + base verb).

questions.question: The laptop is _____ than the other two.
questions.explanation: 'Rather more expensive' is the correct comparative form with modifier.

questions.question: Although there were ten beautiful bags in the shop, Sandra liked _____ of them.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is used with 'although' to express a negative choice between two items.

questions.question: Enrolment has increased _____ the new classroom was built.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with present perfect to indicate a starting point in time.

questions.question: Our dog _____ barking since the stranger entered the house.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous ('has been barking') is used with 'since'.

questions.question: We always _____ the lights before going to bed.
questions.explanation: 'Put out' means to extinguish, used for lights.

questions.question: We saw _____ people in the room.
questions.explanation: 'Many' is used with countable nouns like 'people'.

questions.question: Put the books on the shelf, _____?
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences take 'will you' as a tag question.

questions.question: Amira prepared a delicious meal for her _____.
questions.explanation: The plural of 'sister-in-law' is 'sisters-in-law'.

questions.question: The coach advised the two players to cooperate with _____.
questions.explanation: 'Each other' is the reciprocal pronoun for two people.

questions.question: Selfish people always consider _____ first.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun must agree with the subject 'people' (themselves).

questions.question: Their gardener was _____ old to work.
questions.explanation: 'Too...to' indicates excess that prevents an action.

questions.question: To _____ did you deliver the message?
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is correct after the preposition 'to'.

questions.question: Amarh asked Tettey, 'Did you see the new student yesterday?' The correct reported speech is: Amarh asked Tettey _____
options: A. if he had seen the new student the previous day
B. if he had seen the new student yesterday
C. did he see the new student the previous day
D. whether he saw the new student yesterday
questions.explanation: Reported speech requires backshift ('did' to 'had seen') and 'yesterday' becomes 'the previous day'.

questions.question: 'Had they completed the project before the deadline?' The correct passive form is: _____ the project been completed by them before the deadline?
questions.explanation: The past perfect passive requires 'Had + subject + been + past participle'.

questions.question: Paul purposely left the door open. The word nearest in meaning to the underlined word is:
questions.explanation: 'Intentionally' is nearest in meaning to 'purposely', both meaning deliberately.

questions.question: Nobody paid any attention to the workers' demands. The word nearest in meaning to the underlined word is:
questions.explanation: 'Requests' is nearest in meaning to 'demands', both meaning things asked for.

questions.question: The boy's account of the incident was elaborate. The word nearest in meaning to the underlined word is:
questions.explanation: 'Detailed' is nearest in meaning to 'elaborate', both meaning thorough and complex.

questions.question: It was forecast that there would be thunderstorm in the evening. The word nearest in meaning to the underlined word is:
questions.explanation: 'Predicted' is nearest in meaning to 'forecast', both meaning to say what will happen.

questions.question: His dubious attitude has made him lose all his good friends. The word nearest in meaning to the underlined word is:
questions.explanation: 'Deceitful' is nearest in meaning to 'dubious', both meaning dishonest or doubtful.

questions.question: Aminu is full of himself. This means that Aminu is:
questions.explanation: 'Full of himself' is an idiom meaning arrogant or conceited.

questions.question: She tried to throw dust in our eyes. This means that she tried to:
questions.explanation: 'Throw dust in our eyes' means to deceive or mislead.

questions.question: On seeing the angry mob approaching the school, our school prefect told us to take to our heels. This means that the prefect told us to:
questions.explanation: 'Take to our heels' means to run away quickly.

questions.question: The two boys have often been at loggerheads with each other. This means that they:
options: A. are usually seen walking together
C. have often had strong disagreements
D. usually have the same views on issues
questions.explanation: 'At loggerheads' means in strong disagreement or conflict.

questions.question: I learnt to paddle my own canoe. This means that I:
options: A. am independent and need no help from others
B. do not interfere in other people's matters
C. have no help in my fishing business
D. work hard to feed myself and my family
questions.explanation: 'Paddle my own canoe' means to be self-reliant and independent.

questions.question: The policeman was reported to have concealed the evidence, but _____ it to the jury.
questions.explanation: 'Disclosed' is the opposite of 'concealed', meaning to reveal.

questions.question: He loves taking hasty decisions so he never makes _____ moves.
questions.explanation: 'Calculated' is the opposite of 'hasty', meaning carefully planned.

questions.question: Those children think their uncle is miserly yet he is _____ to strangers.
questions.explanation: 'Generous' is the opposite of 'miserly', meaning willing to give.

questions.question: Though we expected _____, the judge handled the case with partiality.
questions.explanation: 'Fairness' is the opposite of 'partiality', meaning treating everyone equally.

questions.question: The minister publicly rebukes his assistant and always _____ his secretary.
questions.explanation: 'Commends' (praises) is the opposite of 'rebukes' (criticizes).

questions.question: Akuba was trained as an accountant. After graduation, she went out to _____ employment.
questions.explanation: 'Seek employment' is the correct collocation meaning to look for a job.

questions.question: She visited several firms but was _____ in securing a job.
questions.explanation: 'Unsuccessful' fits the context of failing to secure a job after visiting several firms.

questions.question: Afiba, her friend, finally advised her to read the newspapers for _____ of vacant positions.
questions.explanation: 'Advertisements' of vacant positions is the standard expression in newspapers.

questions.question: Fortunately, a reputable company was looking for a _____ accountant.
questions.explanation: 'Certified' means officially qualified, fitting for a reputable company.

questions.question: They needed someone who was _____ in financial reporting.
questions.explanation: 'Proficient in' is the correct collocation meaning highly skilled.

questions.question: The car sped around the curve. Which word has the same initial consonant sound?
questions.explanation: 'Colonel' starts with /k/ sound, same as 'car' (/k/).

questions.question: We won the game easily. Which word has the same initial consonant sound?
questions.explanation: 'Goat' starts with /g/ sound, same as 'game' (/g/).

questions.question: She received a beautiful present. Which word has the same initial consonant sound?
questions.explanation: 'Palm' starts with /p/ sound, same as 'present' (/p/).

questions.question: The city grew quieter with each passing hour. Which word has the same vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Tour' shares the same vowel sound as 'grew' and 'quieter'.

questions.question: The queue moved slowly, yet no one seemed to mind. Which word has the same vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Few' shares the /juː/ vowel sound with 'queue'.

questions.question: Sammy was sad when he lost his mother but he will soon get …………. it.
questions.explanation: 'Get over' means to recover from a difficult experience.

questions.question: The manager was late to office because he …………a flat tire.
questions.explanation: Past tense 'had' is correct in this narrative context.

questions.question: The school band …….. twice a week.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'band' takes the singular verb 'practices'.

questions.question: The law was passed according to strict legal…………
questions.explanation: 'Legal rules' is the correct collocation for laws and regulations.

questions.question: The booking clerk made him ………… a deposit.
questions.explanation: The verb 'make' takes a bare infinitive: 'made him pay'.

questions.question: Although all the dresses were beautiful, she liked …………of them.
questions.explanation: 'None' is used with 'although' to show contrast — she liked none despite them all being beautiful.

questions.question: It is ………to attempt in one day.
options: A. too long and difficult a journey
B. the journey too long and difficult
C. long and difficult too a journey
D. too long and difficult the journey
questions.explanation: The correct adjective order is 'too + adjective + noun'.

questions.question: The rain shouldn't deter you ……… going out.
questions.explanation: 'Deter from' is the correct phrasal verb meaning to discourage.

questions.question: Does anyone ………..how many people are likely to come to the function?
questions.explanation: After 'does', the bare infinitive 'know' is used.

questions.question: No sooner had the minister opened the bank ………….it was filled to capacity.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner...than' is the correct correlative conjunction pair.

questions.question: Will someone please ………..that running tap?
questions.explanation: 'Turn off' is the correct phrasal verb for stopping water from a tap.

questions.question: Her work is always not attractive, ……… ?
questions.explanation: The tag question matches the verb 'is' in the statement.

questions.question: You'll definitely be late to school; ………….. you?
questions.explanation: 'You'll' (you will) takes the negative tag 'won't you'.

questions.question: Her teacher congratulated her …………. her excellent performance in the examination.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate on' is the correct preposition combination.

questions.question: We would not have known the woman's identity if you …………us.
questions.explanation: Third conditional requires 'had + past participle' in the if-clause.
